title: Public Order and Safety (Special Powers) Bill
what_it_is: Public Order and Safety (Special Powers) Bill

sections.label: Female ISA detainee, 18 others
sections.summary: Syaikhah Izzah, a preschool assistant, became the first female Singaporean detained under the Internal Security Act, with 18 other Singaporeans dealt with under the ISA since 2015.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Syaikhah Izzah, a preschool assistant, became the first female Singaporean to be detained under the Internal Security Act.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Since 2015, there have been 18 other Singaporeans like Syaikhah who had to be dealt with under the Internal Security Act (ISA).

sections.label: ISIS-linked plots against Singapore
sections.summary: Singapore has been cited as a target in jihadist publications and videos by ISIS and other groups, with two ISIS-linked plots in 2016, including a foiled Batam rocket plot against Marina Bay Sands.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Singapore has been cited as a target in jihadist publications and videos, by both ISIS and other groups.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: There were two ISIS-linked plots against Singapore in 2016 alone, including the foiled plot by Batam-based terrorists to launch a rocket attack against Marina Bay Sands.

sections.label: POSSPA Bill and POPA question
sections.summary: The Infrastructure Protection Act was passed to enhance security for critical buildings, and MHA is introducing the POSSPA Bill to give Police powers for serious incidents like terrorist attacks, raising the question of whether POPA already provides such powers.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The Infrastructure Protection Act was passed to enhance the security for critical buildings.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Now, MHA is introducing the Public Order and Safety (Special Powers) Bill (POSSPA) to ensure that the Police have the necessary powers to be able to deal effectively with serious incidents, such as a terrorist attack.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Do we not already have the Public Order (Preservation) Act (POPA) that gives special powers to deal with serious public order incidents?

sections.label: Bombings killed three, injured 260
sections.summary: The bombings killed three people and injured about 260.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The bombings killed three and injured about 260.

sections.label: Watertown manhunt and POPA
sections.summary: Had the Watertown manhunt taken place in Singapore, POPA could not have been activated because there was no public disorder.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Had the Watertown manhunt taken place in Singapore, POPA could not have been activated because there was no public disorder.

sections.label: Charlie Hebdo and POPA inadequacy
sections.summary: Had the Charlie Hebdo incident taken place in Singapore, POPA would be inadequate even if its scope were expanded to apply to a terrorist attack.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Had the Charlie Hebdo incident taken place in Singapore, POPA would be inadequate, even if we expanded its scope to apply to a terrorist attack.

sections.label: Repeal POPA, replace with POSSPA
sections.summary: MHA proposes repealing POPA and replacing it with POSSPA, expanding its scope beyond public order to serious incidents affecting public safety, such as terrorist attacks.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: MHA is, therefore, proposing to repeal POPA and replace it with POSSPA.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: POSSPA will expand the scope of POPA beyond public order, to enable the Police to also use it for serious incidents affecting public safety, such as a terrorist attack.

sections.label: Serious incidents definition
sections.summary: Serious incidents include large-scale public disorder, terrorist acts and acts of serious violence affecting the public.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In addition to large-scale public disorder, "serious incidents" include terrorist acts and acts of serious violence affecting the public.

sections.label: Commissioner's Communications Stop Order
sections.summary: Clause 30 empowers the Commissioner of Police to issue a Communications Stop Order requiring a person to stop making or communicating films, pictures, text or audio messages about law enforcement operations in the target area.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Clause 30 empowers the Commissioner of Police to issue a Communications Stop Order (CSO) which requires a person to stop making or communicating films or pictures of the target area, and to stop communicating text or audio messages about law enforcement operations in the target area.

sections.label: Breach of CSO penalties
sections.summary: A breach of the CSO is an offence carrying up to two years' imprisonment, or a fine of up to $20,000, or both.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: A breach of the CSO is an offence which carries up to two years' imprisonment, or a fine of up to $20,000, or both.

sections.label: UAV powers and telco Direction
sections.summary: POSSPA powers let Police take down UAVs and AVs in the target area, and Clause 32 lets the Minister issue a Direction to telcos instead of the defunct Telecommunication Authority of Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The additional powers in POSSPA will enable the Police to prevent compromising security operations, by taking down any UAVs and AVs in and around the target area.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Clause 32 updates the existing POPA section 9, which allows the Minister to issue a Direction to withdraw telecommunication services in a target area.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Instead of issuing the Direction to the now-defunct Telecommunication Authority of Singapore, it empowers the Minister to issue the Direction to the Telecommunication Licensees (telcos) instead.

sections.label: SAF servicemen powers and conditions
sections.summary: The Bill retains SAF servicemen's powers, but an Amendment will move these provisions to the SAF Act, with POSSPA powers exercisable only under stated conditions, while Police lead the response.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: This empowerment of SAF servicemen remains essential, and the Bill retains this, with an updated suite of powers needed by SAF servicemen.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: However, I will be introducing a Notice of Amendment later at the Committee stage to move these provisions for authorising SAF servicemen from POSSPA to the SAF Act.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: This is to ensure a clearly defined command and control by the Ministry of Defence (MINDEF) and SAF over all deployments of SAF servicemen in support of civilian authorities, including the POSSPA powers which SAF servicemen can exercise.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The POSSPA powers can only be exercised by SAF servicemen if: (a) an Activation Order under POSSPA has been issued; and (b) the Police requests for assistance from SAF; and (c) after the Minister for Defence issues the relevant orders under the SAF Act.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: It is clear however, that the Police will lead and coordinate the overall response, with the assistance of SAF servicemen.

sections.label: Lethal weapons powers expanded
sections.summary: Clauses 18, 19, 20 and 48 expand Police use of lethal weapons for cordons, road closures, dispersing processions and arrests.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Clause 18 will expand this to allow the Police to use lethal weapons as reasonably necessary to prevent persons, vehicles or vessels from entering the cordoned area or to remove them from the cordoned area.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Similarly, clauses 19 and 20 allow the use of lethal weapons as reasonably necessary to enforce road closures, and disperse processions and assemblies in the target area, for example, to end an armed skirmish between protestors.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Clause 48 will expand the range of offences which allows the Police the use of lethal weapons as reasonably necessary to effect the arrest.

sections.label: Lethal weapons rules and penalties
sections.summary: Lethal weapon use remains subject to internal procedures and rules of engagement, with a maximum two-year imprisonment, $20,000 fine, or both.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The use of lethal weapons remains subject to internal procedures and rules of engagement.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: This will now carry a maximum imprisonment term of two years, or $20,000 fine, or both.

sections.label: Activation Order one-month cap
sections.summary: Each Activation Order lasts at most one month, after which the Minister must make a new Order if needed.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The duration of each Activation Order is capped at one month, after which, the Minister must make a new Activation Order if he assesses that there is a need for a new Order.

sections.label: Safeguards against Activation Orders
sections.summary: Parliament can question the Minister, judicial review remains available, and time is of the essence in fast-evolving incidents.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Members may ask why we have not carried over the provision in POPA section 3 subsection (5), which allows Parliament to annul the proclamation by the Minister by resolution as a safeguard.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Even without this provision, Members can question the Minister if they believe an Activation Order should not have been issued or should have been annulled.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In any case, judicial review of the Minister's decision to make an Activation Order remains an avenue to curb improper use by the Minister of his powers.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In a fast-evolving incident, such as a terrorist attack, time is of the essence.

sections.label: Swift police action and accountability
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Police should act swiftly, effectively and in good faith, and be held to account after the crisis.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Or is a better approach to enable the Police to act swiftly, effectively and in good faith, and be held to account after the crisis is over?

sections.label: POSSPA powers after terror attacks
sections.summary: POSSPA gives security forces powers to respond to serious incidents like terrorist attacks, with safeguards, after studying attacks in other countries.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In other cities, we have seen the impact of terrorist attacks on the public.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We concluded that our laws need to be strengthened.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: POSSPA will give our security forces the necessary powers to respond effectively to serious incidents which threaten public safety, such as terrorist attacks, and protect our people.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: (In English): Mr Speaker, we did not introduce this Bill in a vacuum.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We did so only after studying the terrorist attacks that had taken place in other countries, and the limitations and problems they faced in dealing with the attacks.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: At the same time, in requesting for the special powers in the Bill, we have put in place safeguards.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: But even as we debate the extent of the special powers, let us remember that we will never really know whether our preparations go far enough, until they are put to the test in an actual incident.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: It is up to us to safeguard Singaporeans and Singapore if and when we come under a terror attack.

sections.label: Bases of expanded powers
sections.summary: The expanded powers rest on serious violence affecting the public, large-scale public disorder and terror attacks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The bases of the expanded powers are acts of serious violence affecting the public, acts causing large-scale public disorder, and terror attacks.

sections.label: Bill powers for disorder and violence
sections.summary: The Bill gives powers for large-scale public disorder and serious violence, triggered by the Police Commissioner to enhance Police effectiveness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: And, surely, having access to floor plans is going to be extremely helpful for strategising where and how operations may be carried out.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Therefore, this Bill provides powers to deal with large-scale public disorder and serious violence incidents, which are largely different from normal day-to-day scenarios.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Additionally, this Bill is specifically targeted towards ensuring that the Police can effectively respond to the situation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This can be seen in how the applicability of the expanded powers in this Bill are triggered by the Police Commissioner, that the purpose of the power is meant to enhance Police effectiveness, is a recurrent theme throughout the Bill presented today in Parliament.

sections.label: Clause 15 calibrates by person
sections.summary: Clause 15 calibrates according to the person exercising the power.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Rather, clause 15 carefully calibrates according to the person exercising the power.

sections.label: Drones and media broadcasting
sections.summary: Hostage rescues and counter-terror attacks have been compromised by social media and live media broadcasting, so taking down drones should be considered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Too many hostage rescues and counter-terror attacks have been compromised through social media broadcasting, live media broadcasting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The power to take down drones in the target area should be considered.

sections.label: Communication stop order and rumours
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the communication stop order prevents passing on official updates to quell families' anxiety.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Because this may be for some time, perhaps one month, according to clause 10(2), inaccurate rumours may run amok through lack of accurate information.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Therefore, would the Minister kindly clarify whether the communication stop order prevents a person from passing on official updates on an ongoing incident so as to quell anxiety amongst the families of those affected?

sections.label: Reasonable steps under clause 45
sections.summary: The speaker seeks elaboration on the reasonable steps management or a company officer must take to absolve liability under clause 45(2)(b).

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: These offences are predicated on the activation order.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Therefore, I would like to seek an elaboration on what, I quote, "all reasonable steps" that must be taken by management or an officer of a company to absolve liability under clause 45(2)(b) are.

sections.label: Police powers not disproportionate
sections.summary: The speaker says they do not think the Police are being given disproportionate powers here.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In my view, the way I deal with this tension is that I do not think the Police are being given disproportionate powers here.

sections.label: Support for the Bill
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Bill, saying the Police should not be unprepared or left without what they need to quell a threat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: And my core position is this: we do not want the Police to be unprepared, left inadequately protected because the Police officers are bereft of what they need to quell a threat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I support this Bill for it is needed to protect Singapore and Singaporeans.

sections.label: Draconian powers in grave danger
sections.summary: Parliament is asked to approve draconian powers for law enforcement only where there is imminent and grave danger to safety and security.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Parliament is being asked to approve very draconian powers to be given to law enforcement and supporting forces, but only in situations where there is an imminent and grave danger to the safety and security of the people in Singapore.

sections.label: Minister's Activation Order clause 8
sections.summary: Under clause 8 the Minister can issue an Activation Order if a serious incident has occurred, is occurring or is threatened.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Under the Bill, the Minister can issue an Activation Order under clause 8 if he is of the opinion that a serious incident has occurred, is occurring or is threatened, and that the use of the Special Powers under the Bill would be necessary to achieve the objectives of preventing the occurrence, reducing its impact, or controlling and restoring public order.

sections.label: Definition of serious incident
sections.summary: Clause 3 defines serious incident to include terrorism-related offences, serious violence, and acts causing large-scale public disorder.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Clause 3 defines "serious incident" to include not only terrorism-related offences and acts of serious violence, but also acts "causing large-scale public disorder".

sections.label: Illustration of growing sit-down protest
sections.summary: Illustration (d) covers a sit-down peaceful protest that grows until paths, roads and normal business are impeded.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Illustration (d) covers a sit-down peaceful protest that grows in size such that there is impediment to paths, roads and normal business.

sections.label: Communications Stop Order powers
sections.summary: The Commissioner of Police can issue a CSO banning making, exhibiting or communicating relevant films, pictures, texts or audio messages.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In addition, it seems to me that in these scenarios, any law enforcement operation would not be tactically sensitive to warrant the use of Special Powers, such as the Communications Stop Order (CSO), a topic I shall deal with next.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It is stated that the Commissioner of Police can issue a CSO to ban the making of relevant films or pictures, and to ban exhibiting or communicating any relevant film or picture, or a relevant text or audio message.

sections.label: TV footage in past incidents
sections.summary: Past incidents show TV footage gave perpetrators live information, while footage taken at scenes prevented fake news and revealed truth afterwards.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Past incidents, such as the Mumbai attack in 2008, have shown that TV footage of ongoing operations had given perpetrators live information on the presence and tactics of law enforcement, enabling them to anticipate the actions of law enforcement forces.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, on the other hand, it has also been proven in past incidents that footage or photographs taken at the scene of major incidents prevented fake news and enabled the truth to emerge, after the incidents were over.

sections.label: Ban on making films
sections.summary: A ban on making relevant films and pictures does not promote fact-finding and accountability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A ban on making relevant films and pictures does not promote fact-finding and accountability.

sections.label: Concerns about CSO compromise
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Government would be slow to prosecute films adding value to post-review investigations, and asks for a more constructive approach to unofficial recordings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, even if the offence of making films needs to be on the books in the Government's assessment, I would hope that the Government would be slow to prosecute if the film or picture adds value to post-review investigations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, Sir, in summary, I still have my concerns about the compromise we are making in the CSOs and I would ask the Government to adopt a more constructive approach towards unofficial recordings of major incidents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These powers will include stop and search powers, requisitioning powers, powers to set up and enforce cordons and curfews.

sections.label: Sufficiency of CPC and POA
sections.summary: The question asks why powers under the CPC or POA might be insufficient to cover an illustration (d) situation, making it necessary under clause 3.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can the Second Minister share with the House why she thinks that the powers under the Criminal Procedure Code (CPC) or POA might be insufficient to cover an illustration (d) situation and, therefore, it is necessary to include this illustration as an example of the "serious incident" under clause 3?

sections.label: Minister's decision and POPA contrast
sections.summary: The Minister's decision requires no approval from another arm of Government or independent body, unlike section 3(5) of POPA requiring parliamentary concurrence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I would also note that the decision of the Minister does not require approval from another arm of the Government or an independent body.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is in contrast to section 3(5) of POPA which this Bill seeks to replace, where every proclamation of a dangerous area must be presented to Parliament for their concurrence.

sections.label: Activation Order publication and offences
sections.summary: Clause 8(3) requires an Activation Order to be published but failure to publish does not invalidate it, and asks whether an individual who refuses to obey a Police Officer is guilty of an offence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Further, under clause 8(3), an Activation Order must be published but a failure to publish does not invalidate the Order.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Moreover, if there is an incident where an Order is not published and a Police Officer uses his special powers on an individual who does not know that this Order has been there, and subsequently refuses to obey the instructions of the Police Officer, is such an individual guilty of an offence under the Act?

sections.label: Media leaks and CSO restrictions
sections.summary: The Bill lacks guidelines preventing traditional media leaks, and clauses 30(1)(b) and 31(2)(b) may restrict informing loved ones and allow orders to delete photos or videos.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Yet, there is an absence of guidelines or provision in this Bill that regulate or prevent the traditional media from leaking information through live broadcasts that may impede security operations, which appears to be the mischief that a CSO seeks to address.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Under clause 30(1)(b), the exhibiting and communicating by any person of a relevant text may be banned during the period which the CSO is in force.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If individuals near the vicinity are trying to inform their loved ones of their safety or to warn their loved ones to avoid the area of the serious incident, how are such individuals able to do so?

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Also, what if an individual takes a photo or a video of an abuse of power by Police Officers, under clause 31(20(b), the Police Officer can order that individual to delete that video or photo.

sections.label: Personal use and intention offences
sections.summary: It seems disproportionate to make a person liable for personal use material with no harm, and clause 38(2) seems to displace intention for publishing prejudicial material.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If, for instance, an individual types something on his phone, or writes something with no intention to publish it and merely for personal use, it seems disproportionate to say that such a person is liable of an offence, especially when no potential harm is caused by mere possession.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Thirdly, clause 38(2) seems to displace the element of intention for an offence relating to publishing material prejudicial to public order.

sections.label: Batam terrorist plot foiled
sections.summary: In August 2016, Indonesian authorities foiled a Batam-based terrorist group's plot to launch a rocket attack against Marina Bay Sands from Batam.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In August 2016, the Indonesian authorities foiled a plot by a Batam-based terrorist group, which had intended to launch a rocket attack against the Marina Bay Sands, using Batam as a launch point.

sections.label: Minister's Activation Order powers
sections.summary: The Minister for Home Affairs may issue an Activation Order after a serious incident, describing the incident, specifying its period, and authorising the Commissioner of Police to exercise special powers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Under the Bill, the Minister for Home Affairs is empowered to issue an Activation Order if a serious incident affecting public safety has occurred.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Such an order must describe the general nature of the incident, specify the period or periods during which the activation order has effect, and authorise the Commissioner of Police to exercise the special powers under the provision of this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The Commissioner of Police is given the flexibility to then decide the targets of special powers, depending on the evolving operational needs.

sections.label: POSSPA in counterterrorism efforts
sections.summary: The POSSPA Bill is part of the Government's ongoing counterterrorism efforts, following the POA Bill and Infrastructure Protection Bill passed last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The POSSPA Bill is an important part of the Government's ongoing counterterrorism efforts, coming after the POA Bill and the Infrastructure Protection Bill which were passed last year.

sections.label: Terrorism threat to Singapore
sections.summary: MHA reported last year that the terrorism threat to Singapore remained the highest in recent years.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Last year, MHA had reported that the terrorism threat to Singapore remained the highest in recent years.

sections.label: Police powers during terror incidents
sections.summary: The Bill lets the Commissioner of Police make a CSO during ongoing security operations, expands Police powers, and bars images and messages in affected areas.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: When there is an such incident of terror, the Bill will allow the Commissioner of Police to make a CSO while security operations are ongoing, therefore, Police powers are proposed to be expanded to deal with terror attacks and serious incidents.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In addition, the measure of barring the public from taking images and banning text or audio messages from the affected area is essential to ensure that no public disorder might arise due to misinformation.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, what constitutes serious incident that provides the authorities with the special power to block all communication and filming and use of social media?

sections.label: Awareness of the new Bill
sections.summary: A member called on the Ministry to create awareness of the new Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Lastly, I call on the Ministry to create awareness of the new Bill.

sections.label: Defining serious incidents and thresholds
sections.summary: A member asked why acts causing large-scale public disorder are defined as serious incidents like terrorism, and what the high threshold for special powers is.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In that light, can the Minister clarify why "acts causing large-scale public disorder" under part (c) of clause 3 are defined as a "serious incident" on the same scale as violent acts of terrorism?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Bill proposes that the Police be given the same set of powers, whether it is dealing with acts of terrorism, or sit-down demonstrations which attract a large group of sympathisers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I do understand that there is a concern that these assemblies might lead to violence and injuries, but can the Minister clarify what exactly is the "high threshold" for the activation of the special powers spelt out in the Bill?

sections.label: Enhanced Police stop and question powers
sections.summary: Some members of the public may find it excessive to let Police stop and question individuals, with fines, imprisonment or force for non-compliance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For some members of the public, it may also seem excessive, in these cases, to allow the Police enhanced powers to stop and question individuals within the incident areas, and, if the individual does not comply, to issue a fine of up to $20,000, or two years' imprisonment, or in clauses 18, 19 and 20, to use force, including lethal weapons, to ensure compliance with orders.

sections.label: Police use of lethal weapons
sections.summary: Clauses 18, 19, 20 and 48 allow the Police to use force as reasonably necessary, including lethal weapons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In clauses 18, 19, 20 and 48, the Police may "use force as is reasonably necessary", "including the use of lethal weapons".

sections.label: Police misconduct reporting and terror threat
sections.summary: MHA clarified the public should lodge a Police report or report to the Ministry on alleged Police misconduct when POSSPA is activated, and the Bill is timely as Singapore is cited by terrorist groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: MHA has since clarified that if members of the public have any allegations of misconduct or abuse of powers by Police Officers, when POSSPA has been activated, they should lodge a Police report or report directly to the Ministry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister provide more clarity on this issue?

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: These underscore how the current Bill is timely, necessary and important, particularly since Singapore has been cited as a target in jihadist publications and videos, by both ISIS and other terrorist groups.

sections.label: Commissioner extending road closure and curfew
sections.summary: A Police Officer can close a road or order a curfew for up to 24 hours under the Bill, and the Commissioner of Police can extend it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Fourthly, a Police Officer can close a road under section 19 of the Bill or order a curfew under section 21, for up to 24 hours, but the Commissioner of Police can extend it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: For how long can the Commissioner of Police extend it?

sections.label: Penalty for breaching a CSO
sections.summary: Breaching a CSO carries a penalty of up to S$20,000 and/or two years' imprisonment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Breaching a CSO carries a penalty of up to S$20,000 and/or two years’ imprisonment.

sections.label: Little India riot and SQ117 hijacking
sections.summary: The question asks whether the 2013 Little India riot or the 1991 hijacking of SQ117 by four terrorists would require such special powers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Specifically, would the Little India riot in 2013 or the hijacking of SQ117 by four terrorists in 1991 require such special powers?

sections.label: POPA 1958 and today's threats
sections.summary: POPA was enacted in 1958 to give Police special powers for large-scale communal riots, but much of its powers are no longer adequate for today's threats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: POPA was enacted in 1958 to provide the Police with the special powers to deal with large-scale communal riots which were the key threat to Singapore then.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, much of the powers in the Act are no longer adequate to deal with today's threats.

sections.label: Internal guidelines governing special powers
sections.summary: The Government has articulated broad principles governing internal guidelines, including lethal force, the two-tier unlocking process, and the Commissioner unlocking individual powers based on needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, I am heartened that the Government has articulated the broad principles that govern these internal guidelines, especially on the application of lethal force, the two-tier unlocking process of the powers in the law and the need by the Commissioner to unlock individual powers based on the needs.

sections.label: Sharing attack news with family
sections.summary: A member asks the Minister to clarify whether sharing text messages about an attack with friends and family on closed networks is forbidden.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: And I appreciate the Second Minister for Home Affairs for clarifying that the victims of terrorist attacks are not prohibited on sending information to security agencies of their situation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But I would like the Minister to clarify whether sharing with friends and families on closed networks is also forbidden, perhaps not video, but text messages indicating that there is an attack and please stay away.

sections.label: Reminding public of communication limits
sections.summary: A member suggests reminding people at the onset of a serious terrorist incident that the law and communication limitation are in place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Perhaps, we can remind people at the onset of any serious terrorist incident that such a law is in place and the communication limitation is also in place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: And this is because, while a limitation of communications is necessary, this provision goes against the initial instinct that many people have to share such information with their loved ones in times of crises.

sections.label: Bill enhances Police powers
sections.summary: The Bill enhances Police powers to deal with serious incidents and security threats, including powers to protect the integrity of tactical operations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Where practicable and instructive, we must learn and implement policies and procedures that can best protect our residents and officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: This Bill is important in enhancing the powers of the Police to deal with serious incidents and security threats, including terrorist attacks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The special powers proposed in this Bill will help Police Officers to carry out these very difficult jobs to save lives and neutralise threats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: In particular, the powers to protect the integrity of tactical operations are critical for operational success.

sections.label: Concerns on CSO transparency
sections.summary: A member seeks clarification that the CSO will only be activated for exceptional situations and that sufficient awareness of it will be in place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Others feel that this provision will affect the transparency of handling and managing security incidents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: These concerns are valid, and I seek the Minister's clarification and reassurance that the CSO will only be activated for exceptional situations where operational secrecy and integrity are critical to saving lives and protecting property, and that sufficient awareness and visibility will be in place to show that a CSO is in place.

sections.label: Social media complicates operational terrain
sections.summary: The operational terrain is more complex because of social media channels, so the CSO is critical to protecting lives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: However, the operational terrain today is a lot more complex because of social media channels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Thus, the CSO is critical to protecting lives.

sections.label: Police orders to site operators
sections.summary: Police can order site operators to assist operations and investigation and suspend their operation, and MHA should explain their duty under this clause.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: When an incident occurs, the Police will be able to order the operators at the site to assist Police operation and investigation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Under Police request, they must suspend their operation for the time being.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: When a serious crime occurs, time is critical for enforcement and investigation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Although operators are mostly willing to cooperate, however, there may be exceptions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: I hope MHA can explain to the operators MHA’s requirement and their duty under this clause.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: This Bill is an important link in our anti-terrorism and crime-fighting framework.

sections.label: Novelty of proposed security legislation
sections.summary: The proposal is unprecedented, with Singapore among the first to introduce such legislation, and the Bill does not prevent hostages or witnesses from communicating with authorities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Part of the anxiety expressed so far stems from the novelty of the proposal, which is probably unprecedented.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I understand that Singapore is among the first in the world to introduce such legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I agree with the intent as it aims to protect everyone and it will empower our security agencies to mount an effective response, should we ever need it one day.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We should draw lessons from the 1972 Munich Olympic incident, the 2008 Mumbai terror attack and the 2015 Paris terrorist attack.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The efforts of the security forces in all three incidents were severely compromised by television broadcasts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: With a smartphone in hand, anyone can be a broadcaster, streaming real-time updates, which can potentially provide valuable information to perpetrators and give them a strategic advantage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: What the Ministry could have communicated better and much more strongly is that the Bill does not seek to prevent hostages or witnesses at the sites from communicating with the authorities, especially information about the attackers and their operations.

sections.label: Meaning of serious incident
sections.summary: Serious incident means a terrorist act, serious violence affecting the public, or large-scale public disorder, and peaceful protests are not POSSPA's target.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We have come across such assertions outside the House.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: There are three limbs under the meaning of "serious incident": a terrorist act; serious violence affecting the public; or large-scale public disorder.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In any case, peaceful protests are not the target of POSSPA.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We will only invoke POSSPA if the situation deteriorates, and the threat of large-scale public disorder or violence becomes imminent.

sections.label: POPA used once since Independence
sections.summary: Since Independence, POPA has only been used once.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Since Independence, POPA has only been used once.

sections.label: CSO not for peaceful assemblies
sections.summary: The CSO is not meant for peaceful assemblies.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The CSO is not meant for peaceful assemblies.

sections.label: Powers after Activation Order
sections.summary: Not all powers become automatically available once the Minister issues the Activation Order; the Commissioner of Police must assess which powers are necessary.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: This confirms Mr Christopher de Souza's understanding also.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I have also explained in my earlier speech that not all the powers become automatically available once the Minister issues the Activation Order.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The Commissioner of Police must assess which of the powers are necessary to deal with the situation.

sections.label: POSSPA threshold for demonstrations
sections.summary: POSSPA cannot be used against demonstrations that do not cross the threshold of threatening large-scale public disorder or serious violence.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: POSSPA cannot be used against demonstrations if these demonstrations do not cross the threshold of threatening "large-scale public disorder", or "serious violence".

sections.label: Corporate officer liability defence
sections.summary: An owner or corporate officer who actually gave closing instructions that were inadvertently not followed will not be liable.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: If the owner or if the officer of a corporation can show that he actually gave instructions for the premises to be closed, but those instructions were inadvertently not followed, then he will not be liable.

sections.label: POSSPA force and lethal weapons
sections.summary: POSSPA allows reasonably necessary force for arrests and certain powers, and Police use lethal weapons only if they have no other choice.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: POSSPA allows the use of such force, as is "reasonably necessary" to effect arrests and enforce certain powers.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Operationally, and as a matter of policy, the Police will use lethal weapons only if they have no other choice.

sections.label: Police reasonable force against threat
sections.summary: The Police had to use reasonable force, in this case lethal weapons, to deal with the threat.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The Police had to use reasonable force, in this case, lethal weapons, to deal with the threat.

sections.label: CSO objective on filming
sections.summary: The CSO aims to signal the public to stop making and communicating films, pictures and messages on law enforcement activities in the target area.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The objective of the CSO is to send a clear signal to the public to stop making and communicating films or pictures, stop communicating messages on law enforcement activities in the target area.

sections.label: CSO not aimed at civilians
sections.summary: The CSO is not aimed at civilians caught in a hostage situation seeking information for loved ones, but at irresponsible communication endangering lives.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: This was raised by Mr Henry Kwek and Mr Louis Ng.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I have said in my earlier speech that the CSO is not aimed at civilians who may be caught in a hostage situation and are trying to get information to their loved ones.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The CSO is intended to stop irresponsible communication of ongoing security operations which may endanger lives, such as those of hostages.

sections.label: No action for good faith breaches
sections.summary: No action is intended against members of the public acting in good faith who inadvertently breached the CSO.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: If members of the public who are acting in good faith to provide information to the authorities, but inadvertently breached the CSO, we do not intend to take action against such persons.

sections.label: Police bandwidth and 1958 provision
sections.summary: In a serious incident the Police will not have bandwidth to sort out malicious intent, and the provision has existed since 1958 without enforcement.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In a serious incident, the Police will not have the bandwidth to sort out those who have malicious intent and those who do not.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: And, if I may add, this particular provision has been around since 1958 and the Police have never enforced it.

sections.label: Activation Order duration cap
sections.summary: Under POSSPA each Activation Order lasts at most one month, after which the Minister must make a new order if a basis exists.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Under POSSPA, the duration of each Activation Order is capped at one month, after which the Minister must make a new Activation Order if he assesses that there is a basis for the new order.

sections.label: Special authorisations need nexus
sections.summary: The Commissioner may issue special authorisations only for incidents with a nexus to the Activation Order incident; otherwise the Minister must issue a fresh order.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The Commissioner of Police will only be able to issue special authorisations for incidents that have a nexus to the incident that led to the Activation Order.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: If there is a subsequent serious incident that does not have a nexus to the initial incident, the Minister must issue a fresh Activation Order for POSSPA powers to be used.

sections.label: High threshold for POSSPA powers
sections.summary: Quoting Mr de Souza that Singapore has a good Police Force, the threshold before POSSPA powers can be activated is high, so they are not for day-to-day policing.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I am still quoting Mr de Souza, "The foundation of my argument is that we have a good Police Force." Perhaps not everywhere in the world, but, in Singapore, we can and should trust that the Police will discharge their duties professionally.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I hope Members can be persuaded that the threshold, which must be met before the POSSPA powers can be activated, is high.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: This means that the special powers will not be used for day-to-day policing.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: It can only be used in exceptional circumstances with many conditions attached already, as some Members have pointed out.

sections.label: Publicising authorised areas
sections.summary: The areas where the Commissioner authorises Police Officers to exercise special powers will also be publicised via all platforms where appropriate.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The areas which the Commissioner of Police will authorise Police Officers to exercise special powers in will also be publicised via all platforms, where appropriate.

sections.label: Hansard and Bill interpretation
sections.summary: The procedure creates open and transparent accountability, and explanations in the Hansard form part of the interpretation of the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: And by putting such a procedure in place, it actually places all of us, or even the Parliamentarians here, plus the Commissioner and the Minister, to a kind of accountability that is open and transparent.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I hear what the Member says about illustration (d) and I think the purpose of a debate on legislation is very often to illuminate on what is in the Bill so that Parliament has a record of the intent of the movers of the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: And the explanations that go into the Hansard constitute part of the interpretation of the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: So, whilst I understand the nature of Mr Kok Heng Leun's request, I hope he appreciates that what has been said in this House, in the course of this debate, forms a substantial basis for us to have a proper interpretation of the Bill.

sections.label: Threshold not low
sections.summary: The speaker states that the threshold is not low at all.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: As I have said, it is not a low threshold at all.

sections.label: Definitions support MINDEF command
sections.summary: Clause 2 amendments support making clear MINDEF and SAF command all SAF deployments supporting civilian authorities under POSSPA, updating law enforcement activity definitions.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The amendments proposed to various definitions in clause 2 are aimed at supporting the key change in this Notice, which is to make clear that MINDEF and the SAF have command and control over all deployments of SAF servicemen in support of civilian authorities during a serious incident under POSSPA.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Amendments 1 to 4 update the definition of "law enforcement activity" to include activities carried out by SAF servicemen using powers under section 201C(9) of the SAF Act.

sections.label: Commissioner does not authorise SAF
sections.summary: Amendments 1 and 2 clarify that the Commissioner of Police does not authorise SAF servicemen to exercise POSSPA powers.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Amendments 1 and 2 are needed to make clear that the Commissioner of Police does not authorise SAF servicemen to exercise powers under POSSPA.

sections.label: POSSPA powers via SAF Act
sections.summary: A key change confers POSSPA powers on SAF servicemen through the SAF Act, keeping them under MINDEF control.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: A key change I will be proposing is to confer on SAF servicemen POSSPA powers through the SAF Act, so that the servicemen remain subject to the control of MINDEF and under the SAF Act.

sections.label: New clause amends SAF Act
sections.summary: A new clause 60 amends section 201C(9) of the SAF Act to include selected POSSPA powers for SAF servicemen during an activation order period.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I beg to move, "That the new clause be read a Second time." I propose a new clause introducing amendments to the Singapore Armed Forces Act which is to be numbered as clause 60.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: This new clause amends section 201C(9) of the SAF Act to include the selected POSSPA powers for SAF servicemen to use when called upon during an activation order period.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: A new section 201C(9)(f) will be added which incorporates the types of POSSPA powers that SAF servicemen authorised by the Minister for Defence to support civilian authorities can exercise.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: If there is no Activation Order, the SAF servicemen cannot be authorised with these enhanced powers.

sections.label: SAF Act penalties aligned
sections.summary: Penalties in the SAF Act 201H will be brought in line with POSSPA penalties of up to two years' imprisonment, $20,000 fine, or both.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The penalties in the SAF Act 201H will be brought in line with penalties in the POSSPA of a maximum of two years' imprisonment, or $20,000 fine, or both.
